SAS ROUND(x, 0.01) applies fuzzing, so near-half values such as 1.005 or a fee of 1.255 round up. The PySpark version divides by 0.01 and floors with no tolerance, so floating-point error such as 1.005/0.01 = 100.49999999999999 rounds down. Amounts and fees that land on half-cents will therefore differ.

SAS ROUND applies fuzz, so values that are half a cent in decimal but slightly below it in binary (e.g. 1.005 or 1.255) round up. The PySpark version computes floor(|x/0.01|+0.5) on raw doubles, where 1.005/0.01 is about 100.49999999999999, so it rounds down and gives different cents values.

SAS ROUND applies fuzzing, so a value like 1.005 rounds to 1.01. The PySpark code computes 1.005/0.01 as roughly 100.49999999999999, so floor(t+0.5) gives 100 and the result is 1.00. Half-cent cases in amount_cents and origination_fee can therefore differ.
